families.title: Probabilistic programs: Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and further systems
families.intro: The programs of the Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and Geni papers, against Dice, Alea.jl and Roulette, and on the programs they take Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Scallop, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl. tddlog runs its own encoding of a program's integers (binary, never one-hot) and is asked what the baseline answers: single marginals where the baseline gives single marginals, a distribution's values only where it computes them. Alea.jl's and Pluck's times leave out Julia's start-up and compilation, as Alea.jl's papers time it; the dashed lines add them to Alea.jl's, and Racket's start-up to Roulette's.

suites.title: Circulette's netlists
suites.about: The digital circuits of [Circulette](https://github.com/sandialabs/circulette), a language on Roulette for the fault analysis of circuits: its netlists, and a ripple-carry adder and a multiply-accumulate unit at growing widths. Each gate fails with probability 0.01; given wrong outputs, Circulette asks the posterior of each set of up to three failed gates. Roulette runs Circulette's circulette.rkt, and every other system reads Roulette's export: Roulette+tddlog is tddlog on the ProbLog program that Roulette's [tddlog engine](https://github.com/Tractables/roulette/tree/tddlog) writes, and Roulette+X system X on that program or a translation of it, each timed with Roulette's run up to the export. 600 s a run. PITA, aspmc, Scallop, PSouffle, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl ran too, on Roulette's export (Roulette+X); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Three more instances no system ran: each system had failed on a smaller size.

setup: Four lab machines: one with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, for the Alea.jl and noDice programs; one with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, for the Dice paper's programs, Roulette's programs and the earlier run of Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs; one with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for the bit-blasted programs; and one with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for Geni's programs. A run is one job that holds its machine alone. Programs run as independent jobs in lanes, each pinned to one logical CPU on its own physical core, with the machine's memory split between the lanes. In a lane all systems run on an instance back to back, in an order rotated by instance and repetition, so that the systems share the lanes alike.

The release run, all of its parts at one version of tddlog, each part with all of its systems in the same lanes: the arithmetic, sequence and noDice programs (10 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, 2026-10-29); the networks, the Dice paper's programs and the loop programs (8 lanes, 15 GB a process, three repetitions, 300 s for the networks and the Dice paper's programs and 600 s for the loop programs, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); Roulette's programs (4 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); the bit-blasted programs for tddlog and Alea.jl (15 lanes, 33 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-29 and 30); and Geni's programs, with ProbLog's d-DNNF timed beside the others (16 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-29). Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs come from an earlier run (5 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, 2026-10-12) on the same circuits; neither those systems nor the circuits have changed since. Times compare within a run: on the bit-blasted programs the plots show tddlog and Alea.jl, and Dice's times are in the tables only. The plots of all programs put the runs together.

A program with a size runs from small to large, and a system that runs out of time or memory on one size is not run on the larger sizes of that program; the tables mark those `skipped`, and they count as failures. A failure of another kind skips nothing.
A time is the median of the repetitions, a failed repetition counted as longer than any time: of three repetitions, a system must answer in two.

For tddlog and Dice, the wall time of the process: parsing, compiling and answering every query. For Alea.jl, the time the program reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as the papers time it; the process's wall time, with Julia's start-up, loading Alea.jl and compiling its methods, is the dashed line in the plots and the "process" column in the tables. For Roulette, its run of the program in the process, after Racket's start and the loading of Roulette and the program's imports; for Roulette+tddlog, the same run up to the program Roulette's exporter writes, plus tddlog's run on that program. The dashed line adds Racket's start-up and loading.
